title: Send federal education money to states as block grants without strings
proposal: The chapter says any federal money for education should go to states as block grants with no strings attached. It says this would reduce the need for federal and state officials.
quote: those funds should be block-granted to states without strings, eliminating the need for many federal and state bureaucrats

title: Return student loans to private lenders
proposal: The chapter recommends that student loans eventually be handled by the private sector again. At a minimum, it says the government should go back to guaranteeing private loans instead of lending directly, while keeping Pell grants.
quote: student loans and grants should ultimately be restored to the private sector (or, at the very least, the federal government should revisit its role as a guarantor

title: Make national emergency declarations expire after 60 days
proposal: The chapter says national emergency declarations should end after 60 days unless Congress expressly approves them.
quote: National emergency declarations should expire absent express congressional authorization within 60 days after the date of the declaration.

title: Pass a law to wind down the Department of Education
proposal: The chapter calls for Congress to pass, and the President to sign, a Department of Education Reorganization Act. The law would reform, eliminate, or move the department's programs and close it as a Cabinet department.
quote: should work with Congress to pass a Department of Education Reorganization Act to reform, eliminate, or move the department's programs and offices

title: Shrink K-12 office programs and block-grant or end the rest
proposal: The chapter recommends cutting the number of programs run by the Office of Elementary and Secondary Education and moving some to other agencies. Programs not moved should be turned into block grants or ended.
quote: Reduce the number of programs managed by OESE, and transfer some remaining programs to other federal agencies.

title: Move Title I school funding to HHS as a no-strings block grant
proposal: The chapter recommends moving Title I, Part A funding for lower-income school districts to HHS's Administration for Children and Families. It would be given out as a formula block grant without strings.
quote: Transfer Title I, Part A, which provides federal funding for lower-income school districts, to the Department of Health and Human Services

title: Phase out federal Title I funding over 10 years
proposal: The chapter recommends that states take back responsibility for paying for Title I over 10 years, with federal Title I spending phased out.
quote: Restore revenue responsibility for Title I funding to the states over a 10-year period.

title: End some Impact Aid and move the rest to Defense or Interior
proposal: The chapter recommends ending Impact Aid that is not tied to students. Impact Aid that follows students would move to the Defense Department's school agency or the Bureau of Indian Education.
quote: Move student-driven Impact Aid programs to the Department of Defense Education Authority (DoDEA) or the Department of Interior's Bureau of Indian Education.

title: Move Indian education programs to the Bureau of Indian Education
proposal: The chapter recommends moving all Indian education programs to the Interior Department's Bureau of Indian Education. This includes the tribal career and technical education program and vocational rehabilitation grants for Native American students.
quote: Transfer all Indian education programs to the Bureau of Indian Education.

title: Make D.C. school vouchers universal and move them to HHS
proposal: The chapter recommends expanding the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship Program into a universal, formula-funded program open to all students regardless of income. It says the program should move to HHS.
quote: should be expanded into a universal program, formula-funded, and moved to the Department of Health and Human Services.

title: Move career, technical and adult education programs to Labor
proposal: The chapter recommends moving the programs of the Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education to the Department of Labor.
quote: Transfer the Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education's few programs to the Department of Labor

title: Turn special education (IDEA) funding into a block grant run by HHS
proposal: The chapter recommends turning most IDEA special education money into a no-strings formula block grant for students with disabilities. HHS's Administration for Community Living would send it directly to local school districts.
quote: Most IDEA funding should be converted into a no-strings formula block grant targeted at students with disabilities

title: Phase out earmarks for special disability institutions
proposal: The chapter recommends phasing out special funding earmarks for certain institutions now funded through the special education office.
quote: Phase out earmarks for a variety of special institutions, as originally envisioned.

title: Move disability discrimination enforcement staff to Justice
proposal: The chapter recommends that any special education office resources used to enforce laws against disability discrimination move to the Department of Justice along with the Office for Civil Rights.
quote: against discrimination of individuals with disabilities, those assets should be moved to the Department of Justice (DOJ) along with the Office for Civil Rights (OCR).

title: Eliminate or move postsecondary programs to the Labor Department
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to end the Office of Postsecondary Education's programs or move them to the Employment and Training Administration at the Department of Labor.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to eliminate or move OPE programs to ETA at the Department of Labor.

title: Limit college institutional aid to HBCUs and tribal colleges
proposal: The chapter recommends that federal funding to colleges be given as block grants and limited to Historically Black Colleges and Universities and tribally controlled colleges.
quote: Funding to institutions should be block-granted and narrowed to Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and tribally controlled colleges.

title: Move national security education programs to the State Department
proposal: The chapter recommends moving postsecondary programs considered important to national security to the Department of State.
quote: Move programs deemed important to our national security interests to the Department of State.

title: Move education statistics to the Census Bureau
proposal: The chapter recommends moving the department's statistics office to the Census Bureau and consolidating education data collection there. Research centers could move to the National Science Foundation if Congress wants to keep them.
quote: Move ED's statistical office, the National Commission for Education Statistics (NCES), to the Department of Commerce's Census Bureau.

title: Spin off Federal Student Aid into a new government corporation
proposal: The chapter recommends reversing the 2010 shift to direct federal student lending and moving Federal Student Aid and its loans into a new government corporation. It would have a board appointed by the President and professional managers, with Treasury handling collections.
quote: work with Congress to spin off FSA and its student loan obligations to a new government corporation with professional governance and management.

title: Move the Office for Civil Rights to Justice; enforce only in court
proposal: The chapter recommends moving the Education Department's Office for Civil Rights to the Department of Justice. There, it would enforce civil rights laws only through lawsuits.
quote: Washington should do so through the Department of Justice and federal courts. The OCR at DOJ should be able to enforce only through litigation.

title: Let needed staff of closing offices move to other agencies
proposal: The chapter recommends that lawyers, accountants and specialists in offices being closed have the chance to join other agencies, if their jobs are found to serve a continuing need.
quote: indispensable to serving the mission, should have the opportunity to join other agencies.

title: Review Biden-era education rules, school meals and loan repayment rules
proposal: The chapter recommends a thorough review of education regulations issued under the Biden Administration, along with changes to the school meals program and the income-driven student loan program.
quote: Thoroughly review the many education-related regulations promulgated by the Biden Administration, as well as the school meals program

title: Rescind 2022 requirements for charter school grants
proposal: The chapter recommends quickly rescinding new requirements for the federal Charter School Program and reducing federal restrictions on charter schools.
quote: The new Administration must take immediate steps to rescind the new requirements and lessen the federal restrictions on charter schools.

title: Drop the nonbinary category from civil rights school data
proposal: The chapter recommends reversing changes that add a nonbinary sex category to the Civil Rights Data Collection and drop some single-sex sports data. It calls for a new data collection tied to the office's legal enforcement role.
quote: rescind these changes, which add a new “nonbinary” sex category to OCR'S data collection

title: Rescind 2023 loan forgiveness rules
proposal: The chapter recommends starting negotiated rulemaking to rescind the rules that expanded borrower defense, closed school discharge and Public Service Loan Forgiveness and banned certain arbitration agreements.
quote: The new Administration must quickly commence negotiated rulemaking and propose that the department rescind these regulations.

title: Withdraw 2022 guidance letters on college accreditation
proposal: The chapter recommends rescinding two 2022 Dear Colleague Letters and letters to accreditation agencies that it says aimed to undercut a Florida law on accreditation.
quote: The next Administration should also rescind Dear Colleague Letter (DCL) GEN 22-11 and DCL GEN 22-10 and its letters to accreditation agencies

title: Block funding to enforce the Biden-era Title IX rule
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to pass a law barring the department from spending money on, or enforcing, Title IX rules issued under the previous administration.
quote: prohibit the department from using any appropriations or from otherwise enforcing any final regulations under Title IX promulgated by the department during the prior Administration.

title: Restore the 2020 Title IX rule and define sex as biological
proposal: The chapter recommends a new rulemaking to rescind the Biden Title IX rule, bring back the 2020 rule issued under Secretary DeVos, and define sex as biological sex at birth. It says this should be announced on the first day.
quote: Commence a new agency rulemaking process to rescind the current Administration's Title IX regulations; restore the Title IX regulations promulgated by then-Secretary Betsy DeVos

title: Amend Title IX law to define sex and add due process
proposal: The chapter recommends asking Congress to change Title IX to add due process rules, define sex as biological sex at birth, and strengthen protections for faith-based schools.
quote: Work with Congress to amend Title IX to include due process requirements; define “sex” under Title IX to mean only biological sex recognized at birth

title: Stop reading sex as gender identity in Title IX across government
proposal: The chapter recommends immediately dropping, in all departments, the interpretation that sex in Title IX includes sexual orientation and gender identity.
quote: abandon this change redefining “sex” to mean “sexual orientation and gender identity” in Title IX immediately across all departments.

title: Review Title IX investigations based on gender identity
proposal: The chapter recommends that political appointees in the Office for Civil Rights review all Title IX investigations that treated sex as including gender identity or sexual orientation.
quote: the political appointees in the Office for Civil Rights should begin a full review of all Title IX investigations that were conducted on the understanding

title: Drop ongoing gender-identity Title IX investigations
proposal: The chapter recommends dropping all such ongoing investigations and telling affected school districts they may reverse policy changes made under pressure from the prior administration.
quote: All ongoing investigations should be dropped, and all school districts affected should be given notice that they are free to drop any policy changes

title: Have civil rights office report on prior administration's actions
proposal: The chapter recommends that the head of the Office for Civil Rights write a report on the office's past actions for the new Secretary, who would then make it public by speech or letter.
quote: The OCR Assistant Secretary should prepare a report of OCR's actions for the new Secretary of Education

title: Tell schools FERPA gives parents full access to student records
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Education Secretary make clear that the FERPA law gives parents full access to their children's school records.
quote: The Secretary should make it clear that FERPA allows parents full access to their children's educational records

title: Review Title VI school cases for disparate impact claims
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing all Title VI civil rights cases to see how many rely on disparate impact claims, and reviewing resolution agreements with school districts to match this policy.
quote: direct the department to conduct a comprehensive review of all Title VI cases to ascertain to what extent these cases include allegations of disparate impact.

title: Stop investigating Title VI cases based only on disparate impact
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Education Department and Justice Department issue joint guidance saying they will no longer investigate Title VI cases based only on disparate impact. It also recommends rescinding any Biden-era guidance or rule on this topic.
quote: the agencies will no longer investigate Title VI cases that exclusively rest on allegations of disparate impact.

title: Issue a rule saying Title VI has no disparate impact standard
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Education Secretary and Attorney General write a regulation stating that Title VI of the Civil Rights Act does not include a disparate impact standard.
quote: a regulation that would clarify current regulations to state that Title VI of the Civil Rights Act does not include a disparate impact standard.

title: Rescind the Equity in IDEA special education rule
proposal: The chapter recommends starting rulemaking right away to rescind the 2016 Equity in IDEA rule, which requires states to look at race and ethnicity in special education. It says no replacement rule is needed.
quote: The next Administration should immediately commence rulemaking to rescind the Equity in IDEA regulation. No replacement regulation is required.

title: Share special education research with state leaders
proposal: The chapter recommends that the special education office gather research on racial representation in special education and share it with state education leaders.
quote: The Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS) should prepare a digest of the best research on this subject and share

title: Bar agencies from cutting school meal aid over Title IX gender policy
proposal: The chapter recommends barring USDA and other agencies from withholding services, such as school meal funding, from schools that do not read sex in Title IX to include sexual orientation and gender identity.
quote: prohibit the USDA or any other federal agency from withholding services from federal or state agencies

title: Replace student loan income-driven repayment plans with one new plan
proposal: The chapter recommends closing all current income-driven repayment plans to new loans and creating one new plan. It would exempt income up to the poverty line and charge 10 percent of income above it, with no forgiveness if Congress allows.
quote: The Secretary should phase out all existing IDR plans by making new loans (including consolidation loans) ineligible and should implement

title: Publish student test data by family structure
proposal: The chapter recommends making student achievement data, such as NAEP results, publicly available by family structure, including in the Data Explorer tool.
quote: should make student data available by family structure to the public, including as part of its Data Explorer tool.

title: House higher education data at the Labor Department
proposal: The chapter recommends moving higher education data to the Department of Labor and adjusting college outcome data for students' backgrounds.
quote: Data collection efforts in higher education should also be improved by housing higher education data at the Department of Labor.

title: End negotiated rulemaking for education rules
proposal: The chapter recommends asking Congress to remove the Higher Education Act's requirement for negotiated rulemaking, or at least allow public hearings instead.
quote: work with Congress to amend the HEA to eliminate the negotiated rulemaking requirement.

title: End the loan payment pause and broad loan forgiveness
proposal: The chapter recommends ending what it calls abuse of the student loan payment pause and of forgiveness programs such as borrower defense, closed school discharge and Public Service Loan Forgiveness.
quote: The new Administration must end the prior Administration's abuse of the agency's payment pause and HEA loan forgiveness programs

title: Combine federal student loans into one program without forgiveness
proposal: If Congress will not overhaul student aid, the chapter recommends one loan program with income-driven repayment, no interest subsidies or forgiveness, borrowing limits, and colleges sharing repayment risk. It also suggests switching to fair-value budget accounting.
quote: Consolidate all federal loan programs into one new program that 1. Utilizes income-driven repayment, 2. Includes no interest rate subsidies or loan forgiveness

title: Revoke the National Education Association's federal charter
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress rescind the congressional charter of the National Education Association, the largest teachers' union.
quote: Congress should rescind the National Education Association's congressional charter and remove the false impression

title: Hold hearings on the NEA's use of federal money
proposal: The chapter recommends that members of Congress hold hearings on how much federal taxpayer money the NEA has used for causes favoring one political party.
quote: Members should conduct hearings to determine how much federal taxpayer money the NEA has used for radical causes favoring a single political party.

title: Ban compelled speech in federally run schools
proposal: The chapter recommends that no teacher or student in D.C. public schools, Bureau of Indian Education schools or Defense Department schools be required to believe or profess any idea. It suggests adding a ban on compelled speech to civil rights laws for these schools.
quote: Bureau of Indian Education schools, or Department of Defense schools should be compelled to believe, profess, or adhere to any idea

title: Bar race-based treatment and teaching of group guilt in federal schools
proposal: For K-12 systems under federal control, the chapter recommends laws saying no one should be punished or benefit based on skin color, and that students and teachers not be required to believe people are responsible for others' actions because of race.
quote: For K–12 systems under their jurisdiction, federal lawmakers should adopt proposals that say no individual should receive punishment or benefits based on the color of their skin.

title: Pass a federal Parents' Bill of Rights
proposal: The chapter recommends passing a federal Parents' Bill of Rights. Courts would apply strict scrutiny, the highest legal test, when the federal government limits parents' rights to raise and educate their children.
quote: Work to pass a federal Parents' Bill of Rights that restores parental rights to a “top-tier” right.

title: Require rules affecting parents' rights to pass strict scrutiny
proposal: The chapter recommends requiring federal agencies to show that any regulation affecting parental rights meets strict scrutiny before the rule becomes final.
quote: require federal agencies to demonstrate that their action meets strict scrutiny before a final rule is promulgated.

title: Let parents sue schools under FERPA and PPRA
proposal: The chapter recommends asking Congress to let parents, and students over 18, sue schools that violate student privacy laws FERPA and PPRA, and recover legal costs if they win.
quote: amend FERPA and PPRA to provide parents and students over the age of 18 years with a private right of action

title: Require parent permission to use a student's non-legal name
proposal: For schools under federal control, the chapter recommends a law that staff may not call a student by a name other than the one on the birth certificate without written permission from parents.
quote: No public education employee or contractor shall use a name to address a student other than the name listed on a student's birth certificate

title: Require parent permission for pronouns differing from biological sex
proposal: For schools under federal control, the chapter recommends a law that staff may not use pronouns for a student that differ from the student's biological sex without written permission from parents.
quote: No public education employee or contractor shall use a pronoun in addressing a student that is different from that student's biological sex

title: Protect school staff who decline to use certain pronouns
proposal: For schools under federal control, the chapter recommends a law that no school may require an employee or contractor to use pronouns that do not match a person's biological sex if this goes against their religious or moral beliefs.
quote: No public institution may require an education employee or contractor to use a pronoun that does not match a person's biological sex

title: Raise the D.C. voucher amount
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress raise the D.C. Opportunity Scholarship amount closer to what D.C. public schools spend per student.
quote: raise the scholarship amount closer to the funding students receive in D.C. Public Schools

title: Loosen rules on private schools in the D.C. voucher program
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress stop requiring participating private schools to give the D.C. public schools test and let them control their own admissions.
quote: deregulate the program by removing the requirement of private schools to administer the D.C. Public Schools assessment

title: Offer education savings accounts to D.C. students
proposal: The chapter recommends giving District of Columbia students education savings accounts funded with part of their federal education money, which parents could spend on tutoring, tuition and other services.
quote: Federal lawmakers should offer District students the opportunity to use education savings accounts.

title: Offer education savings accounts to military families
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress create the same education savings accounts for children in active-duty military families.
quote: Members of Congress should design the same account system for students in active-duty military families

title: Offer education savings accounts to Bureau of Indian Education students
proposal: The chapter recommends creating a federal education savings account option for all children attending Bureau of Indian Education schools.
quote: Federal officials should design a federal education savings account option for all children attending BIE schools.

title: Let families direct their child's IDEA special education money
proposal: The chapter recommends changing IDEA so a child's share of federal special education money can go to families. They could use it for tutors, therapies, textbooks and similar costs, like an education savings account.
quote: consider revising IDEA to require that a child's portion of the federal taxpayer spending under the law be made available to families

title: Let families use Title I money for private learning options
proposal: The chapter recommends giving students in Title I schools micro-education savings accounts so parents can use Title I money for options such as tutoring and learning materials.
quote: Students attending schools that receive Title I spending should also have access to micro-education savings accounts

title: Create a federal tax credit for school scholarship donations
proposal: The chapter suggests Congress consider the Educational Choice for Children Act, which would give a federal tax credit to donors who give to nonprofit scholarship groups. Families could use the scholarships for tuition, tutoring and materials.
quote: This bill would create a federal scholarship tax credit that would incentivize donors to contribute to nonprofit scholarship granting organizations

title: Let states opt out of federal K-12 programs and keep the money
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress let states opt out of federal K-12 programs under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and use their share of federal money for any lawful education purpose.
quote: Congress should allow states to opt out of the dozens of federal K–12 education programs authorized under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act

title: Bar college accreditors from requiring DEI policies
proposal: The chapter recommends changing the Higher Education Act to stop accreditors from using their role in federal student aid to require colleges to adopt diversity, equity, and inclusion policies.
quote: Prohibit accreditation agencies from leveraging their Title IV gatekeeper role to mandate that educational institutions adopt diversity, equity, and inclusion policies.

title: Bar accreditors from interfering in state college governance
proposal: The chapter recommends barring accreditation agencies from interfering in how states govern and lead their public colleges and universities.
quote: prohibiting accreditation agencies from intruding upon the governance of state-supported educational institutions.

title: Protect religious colleges from accreditor standards
proposal: The chapter recommends barring accreditors from setting standards that conflict with a religious school's beliefs or mission, or from interfering in the governance of religious colleges.
quote: Requiring standards and criteria that undermine the religious beliefs of, or require policies or conduct that conflict with, the religious mission

title: Let states recognize or serve as college accreditors
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the Education Department's sole power to recognize accreditors by letting states recognize accreditors for federal aid, or letting state agencies accredit schools nationwide.
quote: removing the department's monopoly on recognition by (1) authorizing states to recognize accreditation agencies for Title IV gatekeeping purposes

title: Consider removing accreditors from federal student aid eligibility
proposal: The chapter suggests considering a change to the Higher Education Act so accreditation is no longer part of deciding federal aid eligibility. The department would instead review schools' compliance with federal accounting rules.
quote: amending the HEA to remove accreditors from the program triad entirely to allow accreditation to return to its original role of voluntary quality assurance.

title: Eliminate Grad PLUS and Parent PLUS loans
proposal: The chapter recommends ending PLUS loans for graduate students and for parents of undergraduates. It estimates this would save about $2.3 billion.
quote: Eliminate Grad PLUS loans (for graduate students) and Parent PLUS loans (for parents of undergraduates).

title: End Public Service Loan Forgiveness
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program, which forgives loans for people working in government and nonprofit jobs. It also calls for ending time-based and job-based loan forgiveness.
quote: The Public Service Loan Forgiveness program, which prioritizes government and public sector work over private sector employment, should be terminated.

title: Limit the Education Secretary's power to cancel student loans
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress remove or greatly reduce the Secretary's power to cancel, forgive or materially change the terms of federal student loans.
quote: amend the HEA to abrogate, or substantially reduce, the power of the Secretary to cancel, compromise, discharge, or forgive the principal balances

title: Narrow borrower defense loan discharges to proven fraud
proposal: The chapter recommends removing the department's power to forgive loans under borrower defense to repayment. Loans could be discharged only with clear and convincing evidence that a school defrauded the borrower.
quote: amend the HEA to remove the department's authority to forgive loans based on borrower defense to repayment

title: Cap overhead payments to universities for federal research
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress cap the indirect cost rate paid to universities for research so it is no higher than the lowest rate the university accepts from a private funder.
quote: Congress should cap the indirect cost rate paid to universities so that it does not exceed the lowest rate a university accepts from a private organization

title: Stop recognizing accreditors that abuse their power
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Education Secretary refuse to recognize accreditors that abuse their power and encourage new accreditors to start.
quote: The Secretary of Education should refuse to recognize all accreditors that abuse their power.

title: Enforce reporting of foreign gifts to colleges
proposal: The chapter recommends enforcing Section 117 of the Higher Education Act, which requires colleges to report foreign gifts and contracts worth $250,000 or more.
quote: Reverse the Biden Administration's refusal to enforce Section 117 of the HEA, which directs colleges and universities to report gifts from

title: Investigate colleges that fail to report foreign gifts
proposal: The chapter recommends investigating colleges that do not meet their foreign gift reporting duties and referring cases to the Justice Department.
quote: Investigate postsecondary institutions that fail to honor their Section 117 obligations and make appropriate referrals to DOJ.

title: Tie federal aid to colleges' foreign gift reporting
proposal: The chapter recommends asking Congress to make colleges' eligibility for federal aid, including student aid, depend on meeting foreign gift reporting rules.
quote: amend the HEA to tie the HEA's foreign source reporting requirements to an institution's ability to receive federal financial assistance

title: Clarify interaction rules for competency-based and online programs
proposal: The chapter recommends new regulations that clarify what counts as regular and substantive interaction between teachers and students in competency-based and online programs.
quote: New regulations should clarify the definition and requirements of regular and substantive interaction for competency-based education, as well as for online programs.

title: Wind down federal area studies programs
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress wind down the Title VI area studies programs at universities.
quote: Congress should wind down so-called “area studies” programs at universities (Title VI of the HEA)

title: Steer area studies money to free-market business programs
proposal: Until area studies end, the chapter recommends a rule requiring at least 40 percent of the funding to go to international business programs about free markets, and requiring recipients to certify they will serve American interests.
quote: require the Secretary of Education to allocate at least 40 percent of funding to international business programs that teach about free markets and economics

title: Reissue executive orders limiting agency guidance documents
proposal: The chapter recommends that the President reissue two 2019 executive orders that treated agency guidance as non-binding and limited enforcement based on guidance.
quote: The President should immediately reinstate and reissue Executive Order 13891: Promoting the Rule of Law Through Improved Agency Guidance Documents

title: Put the civil rights case manual through public comment
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring the Office for Civil Rights' Case Processing Manual to go through formal public notice and comment.
quote: The President should issue an executive order requiring the Office for Civil Rights' Case Processing Manual to go through APA

title: Require grant applicants to promise to uphold the First Amendment
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring federal grant application forms to include a promise that the applicant will uphold the First Amendment in funded work.
quote: requiring grant applications (SF-424 series) to contain assurances that the applicant will uphold the First Amendment in funded programs and work.

title: Drop college degree requirements for most federal jobs
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order saying a college degree should not be required for any federal job unless the job truly needs it.
quote: a college degree shall not be required for any federal job unless the requirements of the job specifically demand it.

title: Remove the list of religious colleges seeking Title IX exemptions
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order removing the archived online list of colleges that asked for religious exemptions from Title IX, and preventing such lists in the future.
quote: The President should issue an executive order removing the archived list and preventing such a list from being published in the future.

title: Be open about FERPA and PPRA complaints
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Education Department be transparent about complaints filed by families under the student privacy laws FERPA and PPRA.
quote: The Department of Education should be transparent about complaints filed on behalf of families regarding the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act

title: Create a parent portal on student privacy rights
proposal: The chapter recommends creating an online portal and resources explaining parents' rights under FERPA and PPRA, including access to school health records.
quote: the Department of Education should develop a portal and resources for parents on their rights under FERPA and PPRA.

title: Expand allowed accreditors for D.C. voucher schools
proposal: The chapter says Congress should remove accreditation rules for the D.C. voucher program. Until then, it recommends an executive order expanding the list of accreditors schools may use.
quote: the next President should issue an executive order expanding the list of allowable accreditors.

title: Account for DEI and gender ideology in federal grants
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring an accounting of how federal programs and grants spread DEI, critical race theory and gender ideology.
quote: An accounting of how federal programs/grants spread DEI/CRT /gender ideology

title: Review results of GEAR UP and 21st Century grants
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring a review of outcomes for the GEAR UP and 21st Century grant programs.
quote: A review of outcomes for GEAR UP and the 21st Century grants programs

title: Reissue the 2018 school safety report
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order to reissue the 2018 report on school safety with updated information.
quote: The reissuing of the report on school safety from 2018 with updated information

title: Report to Congress on consolidating the department and cutting staff
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring a report to Congress on how to consolidate the Education Department and reduce nonessential employees.
quote: The release of a report to Congress on how to consolidate the department and trim nonessential employees

title: Report on the effects of action civics
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order requiring a report on what it describes as the negative influence of action civics on students' understanding of history and civics.
quote: A report on the negative influence of action civics on students' understanding of history and civics

title: Update the Coleman report on family structure and achievement
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order to update the Coleman report to show how family structure affects student achievement.
quote: An update of the Coleman report to show the impact of family structure on student achievement

title: Report how much education money reaches classrooms
proposal: The chapter recommends executive orders requiring a full accounting of CARES Act education spending and a report on how many dollars from each federal education program reach the classroom.
quote: A report on how many dollars make their way to the classroom in every federal education grant and program

title: Pursue antitrust action against college accreditors
proposal: The chapter recommends an executive order pursuing antitrust action against college accreditors, especially the American Bar Association.
quote: The President should issue an executive order pursuing antitrust against college accreditors, especially the American Bar Association (ABA).

title: Eliminate competitive education grants and cut formula grants 10%
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the department's competitive grant programs and cutting remaining large formula grant programs by 10 percent. It estimates about $8.8 billion in savings.
quote: Competitive grant programs operated by the Department of Education should be eliminated, and federal spending should be reduced to reflect remaining formula grant programs

title: Eliminate the GEAR UP college-prep program
proposal: The chapter recommends ending GEAR UP, a federal program that helps prepare high school students for college, and leaving that work to states, localities or private groups.
quote: GEAR UP should be eliminated, and its functions should instead be handled privately or at the state and local levels
